title: Relay allowlist-only ingress — admission at the relay boundary
scope: Rust unit tests over the new admission module plus the generated relay config text and the validator rule. No relay send, pod write or deployment ran.

implemented.admission_at_the_boundary: services/nostr-pod-bridge/src/admission.rs (new, 632 lines) gates EVENT frames before the embedded relay verifies, stores, broadcasts or acknowledges them. An unlisted author is refused with a NIP-20 negative OK ("blocked: …") and never reaches the relay or the pod inbox.
implemented.empty_allowlist_policy: DENY-ALL, applied consistently at both boundaries, with a distinct counter and an audit record under pods/<recipient>/events/audit/relay-admission.jsonl. Relay-OK and authorised-inbox-commit stay separate outcomes and are logged separately.
implemented.config_generator: flake.nix now emits an explicit empty pubkey_whitelist for an empty list instead of omitting the key. nostr-rs-relay reads it as Option<Vec<String>>: omission yields None and the author check is skipped entirely (the relay accepts EVERY author), while [ ] yields Some([]) whose membership test is false for every author. NIP-42 stays on for every non-open policy; the interaction is documented in the generator.
implemented.validator_W039: The message no longer claims a local-npub fallback that no backend implements. It now states the real deny-all consequence for both backends and notes that the embedded bridge still publishes its own locally-signed egress.
